title: Variant Drift Timeline & Root-Cause Navigator
creator: Riley Mendoza
description:
Problem statement:
Teams running canary and A/B rollouts lack a single, time-aware surface to understand how variant-level metrics drift across traffic slices and over time, and to quickly get from a metric delta to likely root causes (routes, users, prompts, model config). Current Console panels show per-variant snapshots and cohort diffs, but there's no interactive timeline, no integrated trace linking, and limited contextual metadata for auto-rollback decisions.

Goal:
Ship an explorer that lets operators: (1) view metric time-series for multiple variants on a shared timeline, (2) highlight statistically significant drifts with configurable sensitivity, (3) pivot from a drift point into an autocorrelation of routes/segments and linked traces, and (4) surface a confidence score recommending manual review or auto-rollback. This improves mean-time-to-detect and reduces unsafe rollouts that increase latency, cost, or semantic divergence.

User story:
As a platform owner, I want to select a rollout and see a timeline of P50/P95 latency, error rate, token cost/unit and a model quality signal (semantic divergence) for each variant so I can spot when one variant starts deviating. I want to click any anomaly and see top contributing routes, recent deployment events, linked traces and a suggested action (scale up, rollback, or watch), with the ability to trigger rollback directly from the panel if allowed by policy.
acceptance_criteria: Explorer shows at least three metrics (latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost) per variant over a selectable time window (5m, 1h, 24h, 7d)
Significant drift points are highlighted using a configurable statistical test (default: two-sided Mann-Whitney U with Bonferroni correction) and a sensitivity slider in the UI
Clicking a drift point opens a right-hand details flyout with: top 5 routes contributing to the delta, sample traces (link to tracing UI), recent rollout events and model config diffs
Variant comparisons support up to 4 simultaneous variants and ability to toggle normalized vs absolute views
Panel integrates with existing auto-rollback engine: when confidence >= threshold and auto-rollback enabled, operator can preview predicted rollback impact and run rollback from panel
All chart interactions are instrumented (analytics events) and linkable via URL (deep link) for incident runbooks
Backend API returns cohort-tagged metrics and sample trace IDs within 500ms for timeline queries under normal load
E2E tests cover drift detection logic, flyout contents, deep links, and rollback invocation mock
Docs + quick tour are published in Console help + a short postmortem template for use after rollouts
technical_notes: Telemetry: require cohort_id and variant_id on request events, propagate to traces and store 1-minute aggregates for each (variant, route, metric). Add semantic divergence pipeline: periodic evals of generation embedding cosine drift vs baseline or reference prompts. Backend: extend rollout-metrics service with time-series query that accepts multiple variant ids and returns aligned series. Drift detection: server-side evaluation produces drift_marks with p-value and delta_pct. Traces: sample up to 10 trace ids per drift window; ensure sample includes high-latency and error traces. Auth: rollback button checks RBAC scope 'rollouts.manage' and confirms on click. Performance: cache aligned series for 30s, limit heavy compare queries to 1/min per project to protect runtime.
implementation_breakdown: Frontend: timeline chart component, flyout details, sensitivity control, deep-link generation
Backend: rollout-metrics query API, drift detection worker, trace sampling endpoint
Instrumentation: new analytics events and 1-min aggregation telemetry
Integrations: auto-rollback gating and preview API, tracing links
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from noisy traffic lead to unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative default sensitivity, require sustained drift over minimum time window and cross-metric agreement before auto-rollback recommendation.
Risk: Telemetry volume increases cost. Mitigation: sample traces, roll up to 1-min aggregates, and provide opt-out for high-cardinality customers.
Risk: RBAC gaps allow unauthorized rollback. Mitigation: require policy check and 2-step confirmation for rollbacks in production projects.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary UI + read-only drift marks): release to internal beta for 2 weeks with synthetic load; Phase 2 (trace linking + flyout): open to small set of customers and usage-based throttling; Phase 3 (rollback integration): enable for teams with dedicated policy and runbook; Phase 4 (general availability): enable default with docs and guided tour
test_plan: Unit tests for drift detector; integration test for aligned time-series queries; e2e for UI interactions; chaos test injecting latency spikes to validate detection and rollback preview; runbook verification with SRE team
